review.brief: Review RM42-account-add-settings-table (tier 1 of RM42), module internal/account. Read the DIFF (0b9897f..HEAD), not the whole module. Validate: (1) module-boundary compliance — no writes outside internal/account except the leader-owned sibling test-fake fix and the gateway doc/test fixes recorded in events; internal/account imports neither internal/tesla nor internal/gateway; no pgtype in any public signature; (2) every doc-pack convention — CLAUDE.md, ai/architecture.md, ai/go-conventions.md, internal/account/AGENTS.md; (3) DB objects match the USER-CONFIRMED design gate (decision D1): account.settings DDL, the CREATE->backfill->DROP COLUMN order, the data-restoring Down, and the PK-only index plan. Any mismatch is a BLOCKER finding; (4) the RM34 status='Active' gating carried forward per decision D2 — EXISTS on GetAccountSettings/UpdateAccountLanguage/UpdateAccountTheme, InsertSettingsIfMissing deliberately ungated; (5) spec/tasks coverage — every tasks.md checkbox reflects real work, specs/account/spec.md matches what shipped; (6) integration tests assert design.md's Test Contract expectations authored BEFORE implementation, not whatever the code happens to do. Test Contract item 1 (backfill) has NO Go test — decision D6 explains why (the harness applies all migrations before TestMain hands over). Judge whether that justification holds; (7) Performance-Profile compliance: read-heavy. PreferencesFor must serve both preferences in ONE query (decision D7) so no render path costs two reads; (8) anti-gaming: no weakened acceptance criteria, no deleted tasks, no self-approved statuses. TEST SIGNALS — assistant-run vs user-reported: go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make migration-guard and make boundary-guard were run by the ASSISTANT and were clean. The TEST SUITE was run by the OWNER, who reported `make test` passing. You must NOT run the suite yourself (Test-Execution-Policy). Judge test quality by READING the tests. NOTE two commits on this branch that are NOT RM42 work: e132741 swept an unrelated internal/gateway/templates/pages/dashboard.go edit into a checkpoint commit, and 1bf8736 fixes a pre-existing stale nav-header assertion at the user's explicit direction. Neither is tier-1 scope; flag if you disagree, do not treat as tier-1 defects.

findings.note: internal/account/db/migrations/20260904000001_add_account_settings.sql -- +goose Down block; tasks.md T1.1 acceptance criterion ('goose down (one step) restores the column with current values and drops account.settings without error (Test Contract items 1 and 5)'). Test Contract item 5 (design.md, 'The Down migration restores accounts.language with the current values') has never been executed or verified by anyone -- not an automated Go test (TestMain in internal/account/testdb_test.go applies only Up migrations before handing control to the suite, so no test exercises `goose down`), and no event/decision in progress.json records a manual `make migrate-down`/`goose down` run either. Decision D6 in progress.json explicitly justifies the missing Go test for Test Contract item 1 (the backfill) but says nothing about item 5, and T1 was still marked status=done with its acceptance criteria stated as met. This is inconsistent with how the pipeline otherwise handles unverified work: T5 (the test suite) was correctly left at awaiting-user-verification until the owner reported `make test` passing; T1's Down-migration claim was not given the same honesty treatment even though running `make migrate-down` is itself gated ('Still gated: ... make migrate-down' per CLAUDE.md §Builds) and so could not have been run by the assistant unprompted. The DDL text itself was user-confirmed at the design gate (D1) and reads as correct on inspection, but an unexercised rollback path on a schema migration is a real risk in a project whose own record (dev DB holds hand-entered, irreplaceable history) treats destructive/rollback DB operations as high-stakes. Ask the leader to either (a) get the owner's explicit go-ahead to run `goose down` once against the test/dev DB and report the result, mirroring how T5's test-suite verification was handled, or (b) if that is not practical here, add an explicit 'not verified, pending owner action' note next to T1 in tasks.md/progress.json instead of an unqualified done, so the state file does not overclaim.

checks.1_module_boundaries: Read every file in the diff (git diff 0b9897f...HEAD --stat, then per-file diffs). Confirmed via `grep -n "internal/tesla|internal/gateway" internal/account/*.go` that internal/account imports neither (one hit is a doc-comment mention, not an import). Confirmed `pgtype` appears only in internal/account/service.go's unexported helper functions (textFromString, nullableTextToPtr, textPtrToNullable, timestamp), never in account.go's public types/interface. Ran `make boundary-guard` myself (assistant-run, allowed) -- clean. Files touched outside internal/account are exactly the three sibling test fakes (internal/app/processor_test.go, internal/telemetry/service_test.go, internal/gateway/handlers/handlers_test.go) plus internal/gateway/AGENTS.md (one-line doc fix) and internal/gateway/templates/pages/dashboard.go (the flagged unrelated change) -- matches the brief's allowance.
checks.2_doc_pack_conventions: Read CLAUDE.md, ai/architecture.md, ai/go-conventions.md, ai/agentic-workflow.md, internal/account/AGENTS.md in full before judging. Checked: interface-first port (account.go), sqlc/goose conventions (pgtype converted at DB->domain boundary, module-scoped db package), unit-suffix rule (no unit-bearing columns added, N/A), account_id-leading index (PK itself), no HTML/no cross-module DB access. No violations found.
checks.3_db_design_gate_D1: Compared the shipped migration (internal/account/db/migrations/20260904000001_add_account_settings.sql) line-for-line against design.md D1/D2's DDL and against progress.json decision D1 (user-confirmed). DDL, CREATE->INSERT..SELECT->DROP COLUMN order, and the Down (ADD COLUMN->UPDATE..FROM->DROP TABLE) all match verbatim. Index plan matches design.md D9: no secondary index, PK-only on both settings.account_id and accounts.id. No mismatch found (see F1 for the separate concern that the Down path was never executed, which is a verification gap, not a DDL mismatch).
checks.4_rm34_gating_D2: Read internal/account/db/query.sql diff: GetAccountSettings, UpdateAccountLanguage, and UpdateAccountTheme all carry the identical `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM account.accounts a WHERE a.id = settings.account_id AND a.status = 'Active')` predicate; InsertSettingsIfMissing has no such gate, mirroring UpsertAccountFromOAuth's existing exemption. Confirmed against generated query.sql.go. Confirmed the integration test (TestAccountSettings_RoundTrip) exercises the Inactive-account case for all three gated reads and the two silent-no-op writes. Correct.
checks.5_spec_tasks_coverage: Walked every tasks.md checkbox (T1-T8) against its corresponding diff hunk; all reflect real, matching work except the unverified Down-migration claim in T1 (F1). specs/account/spec.md's two new requirements and their scenarios were checked against account.go/service.go/query.sql and match what shipped (theme vocabulary, default graphite, normalize-on-read, reject-on-write, settings row guaranteed at creation, single-query PreferencesFor).
checks.6_test_contract: Read service_test.go (TestNormalizeTheme) and service_integration_test.go (TestAccountSettings_RoundTrip, and the TestLanguagePreference_RoundTrip out-of-band-write repair) against design.md's Test Contract items 1-6. Items 2, 3, 4, and 6 are asserted with the exact values design.md authored up front (Settings{Language: LanguageES, Theme: ThemeGraphite}, ThemeHalloween round-trip, ErrUnsupportedTheme rejection, normalized 'neon'/'fr' -> graphite/es) -- these read as contract-first, not back-fitted. Item 1 (backfill) has no Go test; decision D6's justification (TestMain applies every migration before handing over, so no in-process test can seed pre-migration rows) is a genuine constraint of the shared testdb harness, not an excuse -- I judge it holds, and the migration's Up path is still exercised indirectly by every integration test run (a failure would abort TestMain via log.Fatalf). Item 5 (Down migration restore) has neither a Go test nor a documented manual verification -- see F1.
checks.7_performance_profile: Read service.go: PreferencesFor calls s.q.GetAccountSettings exactly once; LanguageFor and ThemeFor both delegate to PreferencesFor, so every caller path costs exactly one query regardless of how many of the two preferences it needs. GetAccountSettings itself is a single SELECT with an EXISTS subquery, both riding PK indexes -- no join, no N+1. Meets decision D7 / the read-heavy performance profile.
checks.8_anti_gaming: Diffed tasks.md and specs/account/spec.md against a clean checkout of the change's own history (no earlier version to diff against since this is the first review round) and read progress.json's task/decision/event history for edits. No task or acceptance criterion was weakened, no deleted checkbox, no self-approved review status (review.status was 'pending' with agent null before this round). The one integrity concern is F1: T1 was marked 'done' with an acceptance criterion (Down-migration verification) that was not actually executed or explicitly deferred the way T5's test-suite verification correctly was -- flagged as a major finding rather than a blocker because the DDL itself is correct and user-confirmed, and running `goose down` is a gated action the assistant could not take unprompted.
